intro: A set of X-ray table models describing the reprocessing of radiation in the circumnuclear environment of accreting supermassive black holes, computed with the ray-tracing radiative-transfer code RefleX 3.0. Each table is a standard XSPEC table model.
provenance: Developed at the Instituto de Estudios Astrofísicos, Universidad Diego Portales, Santiago, Chile, with the support of ANID Beca Doctorado Nacional 21211606.

dataset.citation: Dimopoulos, G., Ricci, C., & Paltani, S. (2026). X-ray table models for the circumnuclear environment of accreting supermassive black holes, computed with RefleX (Version 1.0). Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22082873

overview.value: Cutoff power-law; cutoff energy fixed at 200 keV
ΔE = 20 eV (4 eV retained in the Fe Kα, Fe Kβ/edge and Ni Kα regions)
Rayleigh scattering, Compton scattering on bound electrons, dust grain interactions

flavours.label: SCAT
flavours.description: Scattered photons only; no fluorescence emission

flavours.label: CNT
flavours.description: Transmitted continuum (no interaction with the medium)

flavourRelation: ALL = CNT + RPRC   and   RPRC = SCAT + FLUO

parameters.name: PhoIndex
parameters.description: Photon index Γ of the input cutoff power-law continuum

parameters.name: NHeq
parameters.description: Equatorial hydrogen column density of the dusty torus

parameters.name: CFtor
parameters.description: Covering factor of the torus; ratio of inner cutout radius r to outer radius R, with CFtor = sin(φ)

parameters.name: NHpol
parameters.description: Hydrogen column density of the polar hollow cone, measured along the inner cone surface

parameters.name: Inclination
parameters.description: Viewing angle θ of the system (1 = face-on, 89 = edge-on), sampled in steps of 2°

parameters.name: norm
parameters.description: Photon flux of the input continuum at 1 keV (ph keV⁻¹ cm⁻² s⁻¹)

coneNote: The hollow cone is collimated by the torus. Its inner boundary angle is set to ξ_max = φ + 1° (to avoid overlap), where φ = arcsin(CFtor). The cone has a fixed angular width of 10°, so its outer boundary is ξ_o = ξ_max + 10°. The cone column density NHpol is a free parameter independent of CFtor.
usageNote: The tables can be loaded while still gzip-compressed, as shown above. XSPEC decompresses them into memory each time they are read, so if you fit repeatedly it is faster to decompress once with gunzip and point XSPEC at the resulting .mod file.

usage.label: Typical usage with the ALL table
Reprocessed component with additional soft emission and line components

families.name: RXToPo
families.tagline: Reprocessed emission from a dusty torus with a polar hollow cone.

figure.alt: Schematic of the RXToPo geometry: a central black hole and corona, a dusty torus of inner radius r and outer radius R, and a polar hollow cone, with the inclination angle θ, the torus half-opening angle φ and the cone outer boundary ξ_o marked.
figure.caption: Geometry of the RXToPo model. Figure from Dimopoulos, Ricci & Paltani (2025), ApJ 992, 64.

families.name: RXagn1
families.tagline: Full circumnuclear AGN model including a dusty torus, polar hollow cone, accretion disk, and broad line region.
families.note: RXagn1 differs from RXToPo only in geometry. All other technical details — continuum, energy range, resolution, composition and parameters — are identical.

figure.alt: Schematic of the RXagn1 geometry: as RXToPo, with a central black hole, corona, dusty torus and polar hollow cone, and in addition an accretion disk (AD) and a broad line region (BLR) close to the black hole.
figure.caption: Geometry of the RXagn1 model, adding the accretion disk and broad line region. Figure from Dimopoulos, Ricci & Paltani (2025), ApJ 992, 64.

tool.name: Line-of-sight NH calculator
tool.description: A command-line utility for computing the line-of-sight column density NH_los for the RXToPo and RXagn1 models using RefleX v3. It provides a simple front-end to the REFLEXINO procedure described in Appendix B of Dimopoulos, Ricci & Paltani (2025), hiding the internal complexity of RefleX and enabling quick calculations for individual sources or batch runs.

totalCoverageNote: In both models the total covering fraction of obscuring material is not equal to CFtor alone. The polar cone also contributes solid angle coverage and should be accounted for when computing the total covering factor.

references.text: Paltani & Ricci, A&A 607, A31 (2017) — the RefleX code
